text:

subject: Intro from Dieter - Encord x Nanoflex
text:
Hi [NAME],

Dieter suggested I reach out, as he mentioned you have closer oversight of
the ML pipeline at Nanoflex and thought a conversation with us would be
worth your time.

Quick context: Encord is the data development platform for computer vision
teams in high-stakes domains. We're used heavily across medical imaging and
surgical robotics for annotation, curation, and model-in-the-loop
workflows, particularly where the imagery isn't standard (fluoroscopy,
angiography, intra-procedural video) and label error has real consequences.

Nanoflex's setup looks like exactly that kind of problem:
catheter/guidewire tracking, vessel-level navigation, magnetic actuation
feedback, all from imagery that doesn't behave like a COCO benchmark. Teams
we work with in adjacent spaces tend to hit the same walls early:
annotation tooling that doesn't handle the modality, data ops that buckle
once volume scales, and review loops with no clean way for engineers or
clinicians to flag bad labels.

Worth a 30-min intro to compare notes? I'd share what we've seen work for
teams in similar spots and learn where you are in yours. I have time next
week, do any of these slots work (CET):

   1. Tuesday 5th May: 1430-1500pm
   2. Wednesday 6th May: 1200 - 1230pm // 1500 - 1530pm

subject: [COMPANY]'s $500m round
text:
Hi [NAME],
With [COMPANY]'s $500m round, AI platform decisions tend to lock in fast, especially around auditability and how AI outputs get reviewed in regulated workflows.
If your team is shipping GenAI features across treasury and digital assets, what's the current "source of truth" for evaluating output quality and tracing it back to the underlying data?
Up for a 15-min call next week?

[SENDER] AI/ML Partnerships

subject: Series C scaling
text:
Hi [NAME],

A $75M Series C usually forces decisions on what you standardize vs keep ad hoc, especially around risk and compliance workflows that touch messy data like KYC docs, dispute evidence, and support tickets.

If [COMPANY] is training or tuning models around fraud, transaction anomalies, or ops triage, the bottleneck tends to become data quality and consistent human review, not model architecture.

Up for a 20-min call this week?

subject: AIAH- chat
text:
Hi [NAME], 

Thanks again for your interest in our AI After Hour in SF - I wanted to reach out and properly introduce myself. 

I'd love to grab a quick virtual coffee to share more about future events we have in the Bay Area and learn a bit more about how you're thinking about data and ML workflows. 

My team at Encord work closely with physical AI teams like Synthesia, Boston Dynamics, Dyna Robotics, and Woven/Toyota dealing with multimodal data (doc, voice, image/video, point cloud).

Would you be open to a quick 20min coffee chat? Happy to work around your schedule.

subject: How are you thinking about real-world eval data for VFA?
text:
Hi [NAME] - congrats on the Eka launch! The force-first VFA model is
getting the right attention.

Curious how you're thinking about real-world evaluation as the team scales.
We work with a number of frontier robotics labs (Agility, 1X, Dyna), and
the pattern we consistently see is that the data pipeline becomes a
bottleneck earlier than expected.

For context: Encord ( Series C, $110M raised) supports Physical AI teams
with data collection, annotation, and model evaluation across vision and
sensor modalities.

Would love to share what we're seeing across the space. Open to a 20-min
call next Wed or Thu?

subject: Encord referral by Sai Kishor
text:
Hi [NAME],

I spoke to Sai from your robotics team last week, and wanted to follow up
as he suggested you'd be the best person to speak to about Encord.

After looking at TIAGo Pro and KANGAROO more closely, the overlap I felt
Encord had with PAL is sharper than I realised. TIAGo Pro is positioned
around teleoperation and data generation for AI training, and KANGAROO is
explicitly your embodied-AI / VLA platform: both are exactly the workloads
Encord is built for.

Just wanted to include some more context on Encord and the work we do with
other humanoid and robotics companies to optimise their model evaluations
and data pipelines. A few specific PAL-relevant angles:

For VLA training on KANGAROO: structured observation-action data across
embodiments, contact-state and motion-primitive labeling, and benchmarking
across model versions so you can see where the policy is actually failing.

For TIAGo Pro teleop pipelines: turning raw demonstration video into
timestamped, model-ingestible action labels (grasp type, contact
transitions, sub-task boundaries) without burning research time on data ops.

For multi-embodiment research programs like COGNITIUM and your other EU
collaboratives: versioned datasets that travel across partners, with clear
ground-truth tracking per model iteration.

Would love to have a more structured conversation next week with yourself
and the team. How do some of the following times work (CET):

   - Tuesday 5th May 1500 - 1530pm
   - Thursday 7th May 1000-1030am // 1400-1430pm

subject: Annotation Delivery Partnerships
text:
Hi, we're evaluating new partners for a variety of projects. If successful
from POC, the partner will have the opportunity to work on projects
requiring 50+ full time annotators in production.

Expectations for our partner:
** Project manager required on your end, responsible for project setup and
quality guarantee
** We will provide annotation tools and instructions

Project experiences we're looking for:
** Video Descriptions (C1 English level, typical household chores, no
special industry or knowledge required)
** Transcription in English, French, German, Portuguese, Spanish,
preferably 3+ from this combination )
** 3D Point Cloud annotation
** Image/Video Object Detection vs Semantic Segmentation
** Medical imaging annotation (Surgeon, Dentist, Behavioural Health
Evaluation)

If you have experience and can support on the above, we would like to
schedule a 30 min intro call to learn about your offerings

subject: Mission-critical UAV tracking | Working w/ Skydio, Zipline & Forterra
text:
Hi [NAME],

Multi-camera target tracking that holds up across edge cases is one of the
harder problems in autonomous flight, especially in defense. We work with
autonomy leaders at Skydio, Zipline, and Forterra, so wanted to reach out.

Their teams came to us when:

   1. Tracker failures in flight data were hard to surface and fix at scale
   2. Multimodal annotation (camera + thermal + LiDAR) bottlenecked
   retraining cycles
   3. ML engineers spent more time on data infra than algorithm work

Worth 15 minutes? Tuesdays and Thursdays usually work well for me.
